fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Persona Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the database behind it from one prompt, then changes any part when you ask.
fields.feature_1:
Questions aimed at your personas

Name the groups you think exist and what sets each one apart. Emergent writes questions that can separate those groups, and a second prompt rewords one or adds a choice.
fields.feature_2:
One row per respondent, yours

Each finished survey becomes a row in a database you own, one answer per column. Next year's rows land beside this year's, so a persona that grew shows in the count.
fields.feature_3:
Follow-up questions for one group only

Ask Emergent to show extra questions only to people who give a certain answer. A student who plans to sell sees questions on where they sell; a hobbyist skips to the end.
fields.feature_4:
A persona label on every respondent

Describe a rule in plain words, such as a donor who first came to volunteer, and the app labels each matching row. The dashboard keeps a running count for every persona.
fields.feature_5:
Labels that travel to your CRM

Connect HubSpot or any CRM with an API, and the app writes each respondent's persona label onto their contact record. Sales can filter by persona without the survey open.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the survey link can match your brand. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and build on it.
fields.why_description: Surveys built with Emergent have no response caps. Send the persona survey to every customer, and every reply counts toward a persona.

fields.usecase_heading: Persona Surveys That Changed a Plan
fields.tab_content_1:
Who buys payroll? Office managers, 188 of 412

Plumbline Payroll asks 412 customers for their role and head count. The app gives the office manager persona to anyone in that role at a firm under 20 staff, and the count comes to 188. Finance leads make up 141 and outside bookkeepers 83. The homepage now speaks to the office manager.
fields.tab_content_2:
Planning on Sunday, shopping in pairs

Skillethouse asks 960 users of its meal-planning app when they plan the week's meals. Sunday wins with 402, ahead of 351 who decide the night of and 207 who plan around a diet. A follow-up finds 288 of the 402 Sunday planners shop with a partner. A shared shopping list moves into the next release.
fields.tab_content_3:
231 donors came from an adoption

Every donor on the Hollyburn Animal Rescue list gets one question: what first led you to give? Adopting a pet there leads with 231 of 538 answers. Volunteering accounts for 164 and a social post for 143. The monthly giving appeal now goes to adopters first, timed to the anniversary of each adoption.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pricing help for 96 students who sell

Glazeworks Studio asks students why they take ceramics classes. Of 366 students, 96 plan to sell their work and 270 throw for fun. Only students who plan to sell see the next questions, on where they sell: 58 at craft markets and 38 through an online shop. The studio adds a spring class on pricing handmade pieces.

faq_plan.q: How do I create persona survey questions?

plan.angle: The live SERP is buyer persona question lists (42, 100, 150 questions) and two survey-tool guides; none shows which answers split respondents into personas or what a team changed once the personas existed. This page treats persona survey questions as the few questions that sort real customers, users, donors or students into groups, and shows four surveys built from a prompt that each end in a count per persona and one decision. The how-to gives question-writing practice as plain advice, and the FAQ covers sample size, question types, buyer versus user personas, demographics, who to ask, length, interviews and incentives with no third-party claims.
tab_stories: Plumbline Payroll asks 412 customers about their role and company size; 188 are office managers at firms under 20 staff, 141 finance leads at firms of 20 to 100, and 83 outside bookkeepers, and the homepage is rewritten for the office manager.

Skillethouse, a meal-planning app, asks 960 users when they plan the week's meals; 402 plan on Sunday, 351 decide the night of, and 207 plan around a diet, and 288 of the 402 Sunday planners shop with a partner, so a shared shopping list moves into the next release.

Hollyburn Animal Rescue asks 538 donors what first led them to give; 231 adopted a pet there, 164 volunteered, and 143 found the rescue through a social post, and the monthly giving appeal goes to adopters first.

Glazeworks Studio asks 366 students why they take ceramics classes; 270 throw for fun and 96 plan to sell, and only those 96 see follow-up questions on where they sell (58 at craft markets, 38 in an online shop), so the studio adds a pricing class for sellers.
